FEA-CH-37.text:
Numbers follow a three-digit rule by default: at most three significant digits, four at most, with a scale word, for example 1.23 million, 167.5 thousand or 167 thousand.

Readers never get more precision than the author chose to show. Readouts, tooltips, the Table view, CSV and every export show values at the author's chosen precision; the underlying, more exact source values cannot be retrieved. Otherwise what a reader can dig out would differ from what the author and reviewers saw, and could disclose how precise the author's calculations are.

The author can set more or fewer digits, per chart or per element, and can give tooltips a higher precision than labels; readers then see that precision, and no more. There is no warning at publish time.
FEA-CH-37.note: Dictated by Daniel in the review chat on 2026-10-26: "The three-digit system I had: three digits, at max four, so you can have 1.23 million or 167.5 thousand, or just 167 thousand. If you want to see a table, there should be a way to explore the value that the author decided to put in. By default you should not be able to retrieve the underlying ultra-exact values, because that could show a difference between what the author and reviewer see at first level and could disclose things they don't want disclosed, like how precise their calculations are. The author needs to be able to set more or fewer digits, for example tooltip precision higher than the normal precision. Getting to the underlying data shouldn't give you more detail than the first way you see it. No warning when publishing." Recorded by the lockdown agent at his request.
